messages.subject: bilateral symmetry and PCA
parts:
Hi everyone,

I performed GPA with semi-landmarks and bending energy (gpagen function) and then enforced object symmetry (bilat.symmetry function). Next, I extracted the symmetrical shape component from bilat.symmetry and these were used as my input variables for PCA. I'm curious whether object symmetry has any unusual effects on the results of PCA and whether it is typical to do PCA on the symmetrical shape component, as some of the input variables are perfectly correlated with others. When I look at the higher rank PCs there is no variation left to explain & the eigenvalues become negative.

Nick

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] bilateral symmetry and PCA
parts:
Nick,

shape data on perfectly symmetrical structures, as the ones resulting from a bilat.symmetry analysis, will be definition have less degrees of freedom than a typical GM dataset, because they include landmarks that are redundant with respect to the symmetry axis. That is, in a perfectly symmetric structure, you can perfectly know the position of a landmark on the e.g. right side of the structure by knowing the position of the corresponding landmark on the left side. Thus, although you have digitized and represent in your shape matrix both sides, the real information included is less than that corresponding to the strict number of expected shape dimensions (2k - 4 for a 2D GM digitization). In a PCA this is evident through the eigenvalues and % of variance explained in the last dimensions.

Hope this helps

Antigoni
